subject: Coord: architecture deep-dive + throughput dry run for Acme demo
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: architecture deep-dive + perf targets before demo

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the overview yesterday. We have an internal stakeholder demo next week (May 16) and want to schedule a technical deep-dive with your team to walk through the serving topology and run a short throughput dry run. Two asks:

1) Can we get a 60-minute architecture + perf session to cover model variants, batching behaviour, and failure fallbacks?
2) During that session, we'd like to run a 15-20 minute dry run hitting our projected token throughput so we can validate end-to-end latency and KV cache behaviour. Our initial target is ~45k tokens/sec peak aggregated (burstable) with p95 latency target <= 250ms for single-region runs.

Proposed windows: May 9 10:00-11:00 PDT or May 9 14:00-15:00 PDT. If those don't work, happy to take alternatives.

Can you confirm who from your side should be on the call? We may bring a couple of SREs.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Reynolds
Director of ML Infrastructure, Acme Inc.
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 May 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive + perf targets before demo

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. We can run that session and the dry run. Quick answers up front:

- Attendees from our side: me (serving/runtime), Laura Bennett (console/observability), Priyom Das (load test automation). Markus Klein (runtime kernels) will join for the dry run portion.
- May 9 10:00-11:00 PDT works for us; we can also do 14:00 if you prefer an afternoon slot.

Prep items we need from Acme before the dry run:
- Representative prompt mix and average sequence length (tokens)
- Target concurrency/virtual clients and exact target tokens/sec you want to exercise
- Any IP/network constraints for the load generator (source IP allowlist)

I've attached a short agenda and a draft loadtest-config we propose. Please fill in the prompt mix and return by EOD May 8 so Priyom can finalize the harness.

Attachments: ACME_throughput_agenda_v2.pdf, loadtest-config.yaml

Link to shared folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/abc123

If the 10am slot becomes tight, we can shift to 14:00; let me know.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2028 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive + perf targets before demo

Karthik — 10:00 PDT is better for our execs. One clarification on the throughput numbers: the 45k tokens/sec is an aggregate of 10 concurrent sessions with an average of ~220 tokens per response (we're using a 2:1 request:response token ratio). If you need a target per virtual client we can compute that precisely and upload to the folder.

We also want to validate cold-start behavior for a 30-minute window after a model swap; can you include that in the dry run script?

I'll populate the prompt mix doc and the client target by EOD May 8.

Thanks — Sarah

--
Sarah Liu
Product Ops, Acme Inc.
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 May 2028 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: architecture deep-dive + perf targets before demo

Looping in some internal notes before the call:

- Load generator pool: we can support the 45k tokens/sec target from our dedicated cluster if we reserve the slot, but we need to pin the exact client distribution (we can't safely extrapolate from averages).
- Dry-run plan: 10m warmup (gradual ramp), 20m sustained run hitting target, 10m cooldown + model-swap cold-start check.
- Observability hooks: Laura will enable token-level tracing and the request-id drill-down for the slot; please avoid enabling full payload logging.

Action items for the May 9 session:
- Acme: upload prompt mix and exact tokens/client by EOD May 8 (Sarah).
- Redwood: I will check capacity and reserve the slot by EOD May 8, and upload a dryrun-results-template.xlsx that Tom/Sarah can use to capture observed latency percentiles.

Attachments I will push to the shared folder: dryrun-results-template.xlsx

-Priyom
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 May 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmed: May 9 10:00-11:00 PDT — architecture walk + throughput dry run

Tom/Sarah — confirmed on our side for May 9 10:00-11:00 PDT. Summary and checklist for the call:

Agenda (attached): quick topology review (15m), batching/kv cache behaviour (15m), dry run plan and roles (5m), dry run execution (25m).
Dry run targets: aggregate 45k tokens/sec, expected average seq len ~220, p95 latency goal <= 250ms. We'll do the warmup/model swap cold-start check as requested.
We will reserve dedicated capacity and I asked Priyom to pin the slot. Please make sure your network team provides the allowlist if needed.

Call logistics: Zoom link (in calendar invite). Drive folder contains: loadtest-config.yaml, ACME_throughput_agenda_v2.pdf, dryrun-results-template.xlsx. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME

If anything changes on your side, flag it in this thread. See you tomorrow.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
